reference: Symeon, Dialogus contra omnes haereses, Caput XIV 'Contra gentes impias', approx. cols. 77-78 (Latin: 'arcu enim gladioque virentes, adversus omnem gentem moventur, persequentes, interficientes more latronum, aliena rapientes')
gist_en: Describes the Muslims as armed raiders who attack every nation, kill, seize goods and separate fathers from children.
why_excluded: Call-to-violence and ethnic-group abuse (the 'armed raiders' description of a whole people): excluded by the rule on violence and ethnic insult.

reference: Symeon, Dialogus contra omnes haereses, Caput XIV, approx. cols. 77-78 (Latin: 'neſanda contra naturam Sodomitarum facinora ... usorum copiam sibi colligunt')
gist_en: Charges the Muslims with sodomy and sexual licence, and with a 'paradise' full of lust.
why_excluded: Sexual insult against a people and personal-moral abuse (not doctrinal); excluded.

reference: Symeon, Dialogus contra omnes haereses, Caput XIV, approx. cols. 77-78 (Latin: 'decepti ab homine immundo et barbaro'; Greek 'ὁ δυσσεβέστατος καὶ μαινόμενος Βάρβαρος' cited in the modern Greek reproduction)
gist_en: Calls Muhammad an impure and barbarian man and a most impious madman; the doctrinal claims in the same sentence (apostleship, ascension) are kept in sym_01.
why_excluded: Personal insult ('impure', 'barbarian') separated from the doctrinal content, which is quoted in sym_01 without these words; the insult words alone are excluded.
